textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 9 science · How Forces Affect Motion · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: A force is a push or a pull. Balanced forces cancel and the net force is zero; unbalanced forces change an object's motion.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: A force is a push or a pull. Balanced forces cancel and the net force is zero; unbalanced forces change an object's motion.
beats.speakEn: A force is a push or a pull. Balanced forces cancel and the net force is zero; unbalanced forces change an object's motion.

beats.en: Friction is the force that opposes relative motion between surfaces in contact. It is often useful, but also wastes energy as heat.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 9 science · How Forces Affect Motion · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Newton's first law says an object stays at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless an unbalanced force acts on it. This property is called inertia.

beats.en: Newton's first law says an object stays at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless an unbalanced force acts on it. This property is called inertia.
beats.speakEn: Newton's first law says an object stays at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless an unbalanced force acts on it. This property is called inertia.

beats.en: Newton's second law says the net force is mass times acceleration, F = m a, so the same force gives a smaller acceleration to a larger mass.
beats.speakEn: Newton's second law says the net force is mass times acceleration, F  equals  m a, so the same force gives a smaller acceleration to a larger mass.
